certificate.message: Has completed the De-escalation Basics customer-service module.
certificate.title: Certificate of Completion

blocks.html: An angry customer is on the line. Their voice is raised, and the first thirty seconds will decide whether this call ends with a solution or a complaint. This module gives you a simple way to stay in control when the other person isn't.

items: Hear the real problem underneath the anger
Use the 4-step method: hear them out, empathize, ask, resolve
Choose words that lower the temperature instead of raising it

blocks.html: How this works: read each screen, answer the checks, then handle a heated call in a scenario. Your choices change what happens next.

options.feedback: Exactly. People can't hear solutions until they feel heard.
options.text: Let them finish, then say what you heard in your own words.

options.feedback: Policy first sounds like a wall. They'll only shout louder.
options.text: Interrupt politely and read the billing policy.

options.feedback: Matching their volume turns a complaint into a contest.
options.text: Raise your voice slightly so they know you're serious.

options.feedback: Hold feels like punishment when someone is already upset.
options.text: Put them on hold for two minutes to cool off.

screens.prompt: A customer starts the call shouting about a bill they say is wrong. What is your best FIRST move?
screens.title: Quick check: first move

choices.feedback: Strong. You gave him something today and a clear path for the rest. Most people accept a two-step yes.
choices.text: Say: “I hear you — here’s what I can do right now, and here’s what I’ll get approved by tomorrow.” Then lay out both options.

choices.feedback: Safe, but cold. He heard “the computer says no” — and he’s already looking up your competitor.
choices.text: Repeat the policy word for word and tell him there’s nothing else you can do.

choices.feedback: That just happened — and now you have two problems: the refund, and the way you spoke to him. Words like “unreasonable” always cost you.
choices.text: Tell him he’s being unreasonable and that shouting won’t change the policy.

screens.prompt: It’s minute four. Marcus has calmed down a little, but now he says: “I want a full refund, and I want it today, or I’m cancelling everything.” Company policy allows a partial credit — a full refund needs a supervisor’s approval, which takes 24 hours. What do you do?
screens.title: The refund demand

blocks.html: When a conversation heats up, run the same four steps every time:

items: 1. Hear them out — let them finish. Don’t interrupt, even to help.
2. Empathize out loud — “That sounds frustrating” costs nothing and buys everything.
3. Ask what good looks like — “What would fix this for you?” turns venting into problem-solving.
4. Resolve in steps — offer what you can do now, and name exactly what happens next.

blocks.html: Never say: “Calm down,” “That’s our policy,” or “There’s nothing I can do.” Each one adds fuel.

options.feedback: Exactly. Agreement plus action. That’s the whole game.
options.text: “You’re right to be frustrated — let’s fix this together.”

options.feedback: Close, but it’s become wallpaper — customers hear it as a script.
“Tries its best” defends the company instead of helping the person in front of you.
A transfer right now feels like being passed off, not helped.
options.text: “Let me transfer you to someone who can help.”

screens.prompt: The customer says, “Nobody ever helps me with this.” Which reply rebuilds trust fastest?
screens.title: Quick check: rebuild trust

screens.failMessage: Review the four steps — hear, empathize, ask, resolve — and try again. Calm is a skill, not a personality trait.
screens.passMessage: You stay calm under pressure and turn heat into progress. That’s the skill customers remember.
screens.title: Your results

meta.author: Payne Roberts
meta.description: Second demo course for the e-learning engine. Six screens: content, two knowledge checks, a three-branch scenario with a negative-score choice, and results. Proves the engine renders any valid config.
meta.title: Difficult Customer Conversations: De-escalation Basics
